chunks: Ali, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, who said:

Ahmad ibn al-Qasim wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith عليه السلام, asking him about a believer who dies, and the washer comes to wash him while a group of the Murji'ah are present with him: should he wash him with the washing of the general populace, and not turban him, and not place a palm stalk with him?

So he wrote: "He should wash him with the washing of a believer, even if they are present. As for the palm stalk, then let him conceal it, and let them not see him, and let him exert his utmost effort in that."

key_terms.الْجَرِيدَةُ: the palm stalk placed with the deceased according to funerary practice
key_terms.الْعَامَّةِ: the general populace, referring here to the common non-Shi'i practice
key_terms.الْغَاسِلُ: the one who performs the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِ: the believer, meaning the deceased person whose rites are to follow the prescribed rites of a believer
key_terms.الْمُرْجِئَةِ: the Murji'ah, a sect whose presence creates the need for caution
key_terms.جَهْدَهُ: his utmost effort, meaning maximum care in carrying out the instruction
key_terms.غُسْلَ الْمُؤْمِنِ: the prescribed ritual washing specific to a believer
key_terms.فَلْيَسْتَخْفِ بِهَا: let him conceal it, meaning to do so discreetly

ai.seo_question: How should a deceased believer be washed if non-Shi'i opponents are present during the funeral rites?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on preparing a deceased believer for burial when opponents are present. The Imam عليه السلام instructs that the rites of a believer must still be performed properly, while certain distinctive practices should be concealed if necessary.
